title: Mar bar Amemar
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman says he learned from his father, later sat with Rav Ashi and helped him arrange the Talmud. In [Pesachim 74b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.74b.12) he tells Rav Ashi: “Father would gulp it down.” [Sukkah 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.32b.19) has him saying: “Father called that one a ‘foolish myrtle.’” [In Sukkah 41b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.41b.10) he says: “Father is indeed praying.” In [Bava Metzia 68a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.68a.8): “Father did this”; in [Bava Batra 174a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.174a.9): “Thus Father said”; and in [Ketubot 43b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.43b.2):
he tells Rav Ashi what the sages of Nehardea say. In [Shabbat 45b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.45b.6) he transmits a ruling in Rava’s name.[^4]

notes.text: The supplied הדם literally reads “blood”; the context and myrtle expression support הדס, “myrtle.” This remains an explicit source question. The checked Sukkah 41b confirms prayer, not bowing.

No new primary scalar was returned. Mar reports Father’s practice; Father means his father Amemar rather than an additional speaker Abba. Supplied הדם, blood, is contextually rendered myrtle beside הדס, without proof of a recurring mem/samekh transcription error. The earlier Sukkah41b consultation supports IS INDEED PRAYING, not bowing or roasted prayer. Hyman’s claim that Mar assisted Rav Ashi in arranging the Talmud remains attributed history. All locators, full Rav titles and the Ketubot quotation’s continuation across the unit boundary remain; no whole primary source is newly claimed.

Hyman’s print (vol. III, p. 897) also reads הדם, “blood.” Sukkah 32b directly gives הדס שוטה, “foolish myrtle.” At Sukkah 41b Mar reports that his father prayed while holding the lulav. Pesachim 74b also gives an alternate report in which Rav Ashi himself gulps it down. At Shabbat 45b the consulted text prints Rav in parentheses and Rava in brackets. Hyman’s account of Mar’s role in arranging the Talmud remains his historical judgment.

The speaker in Pesachim and Sukkah is Mar, and “Father” is his father Amemar. Pesachim preserves a second version in which Rav Ashi himself gulps it down. At Shabbat 45b the consulted text shows Rav in parentheses and Rava in brackets as Mar’s authority.
